ψαλλόντων ἱερουργῶν περὶ τῆς Ἱερου- σαλήμ· "6∆εδοξασμένα ἐλαλήθη περὶ σοῦ, ἡ
πόλις τοῦ Θεοῦ."6 ∆ιαμέμνηται καὶ τούτου καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος λέγων, μὴ χρῆναί
τινας ὀμνύειν κατὰ τῆς ἑαυτῶν κεφαλῆς, ὅτι οὐ δύνανται μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ἢ
μέλαιναν ποιῆσαι· μήτε μὴν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶ τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως.
Ὤμνυον γὰρ κατὰ τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων, πόλιν αὐτὴν, ὡς ἔφην, ὀνομάζον- τες Θεοῦ.
Ἀντεστηρίζοντο δὲ καὶ ἐπ' αὐτῷ, ἰσχὺν ἑαυτῶν εἶναι λέγοντες τὸν τῶν δυνάμεων
Κύριον. Ἀλλ' ἦν ἀναγκαῖον τοὺς ὧδε τότ' ἔχειν ὑπειληφότας μὴ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ
βεβηλῶσαι πόλιν βωμοῖς, καὶ θυσίαις, καὶ ταῖς τῶν δαιμονίων ἀπάταις ἐνισχημέ-
νους, μήτε μὴν κατερεθίζειν ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς τὸν ἐφ' ᾧ τεθαρσήκασι, κατευφραίνειν δὲ
μᾶλλον σπουδάσμασιν ἀγαθοῖς, καὶ καθάπερ τινὰ θυσίαν αὐτῷ προσκομί- ζοντες τὸ
ἀραρὸς εἰς εὐσέβειαν. Πλὴν ἀκούσατε ταῦτα, φησί· καὶ ποῖα ταῦτα; Τὰ πρότερα ἔτι
ἀπήγ- γειλα, ἐκ τοῦ στόματός μου ἐξῆλθε, καὶ ἀκουστὸν ἐγένετο. Ἐξάπινα ἐποίησα,
καὶ ἐπῆλθεν. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ, ὡς ἔφην, ἐν ἀρχαῖς τούς τε καλουμένους γνώ- στας καὶ
οἰωνοσκόπους πανταχόθεν συναγαγὼν ὁ θεομισὴς Μανασσῆς ἀεὶ τὸ μέλλον
περιειργάζετο, καὶ ταῖς ἐκείνων βωμολοχίαις συνηρπασμένος, ᾠήθη τάχα που καὶ
εἰδέναι σαφῶς αὐτό· ταύτῃ τοί φησιν ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεός· Ἐγώ σοι καὶ τὰ πρῶτα ἀπήγ-
γειλα, καὶ οὐ παρ' ἑτέρου τινὸς τῶν ψευδωνύμων θεῶν ἐλαλήθη ταῦτα πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
ἀλλ' ἐκ τοῦ στόμα- τός μου ἐξῆλθε· καὶ ἀκουστόν σοι γέγονε, καὶ ἐξά- πινα ἐποίησα,
καὶ ἐπῆλθε, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, εἰ καὶ μὴ 70.1017 προσεδόκησας εἰς πέρας ἥξειν αὐτὰ, ἀλλ'
οὖν ἔγνως διὰ πραγμάτων αὐτῶν, καὶ πείρας αὐτῆς, ὅτι καὶ ἐποίησα, καὶ ἐπῆλθεν.
Ἔοικε δὲ προτέραν λέγειν τὴν ἐπενεχθεῖσαν αὐτοῖς ἐκ τοῦ πολέμου ταλαιπω- ρίαν,
ὅτε καὶ τῆς ἐνεγκούσης αὐτοὺς ἀπενηνεγμένοι, καὶ πικρᾶς δουλείας λαβόντες ζυγὸν,
εἰς τὴν Περσῶν καὶ Μήδων ἀπεκομίζοντο χώραν. ∆εύτερα γὰρ μετ' ἐκεῖνα
συμβέβηκε τοῖς Βαβυλωνίοις τὰ ἐκ θείας ὀργῆς ἐπενεχθέντα αὐτοῖς, ἃ καὶ ἤδη διὰ
πλείστων ὅσων ἡμῖν εἴρηται λόγων. 9Γινώσκω ἐγὼ ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ, καὶ νεῦρον
σιδη- ροῦν ὁ τράχηλός σου, καὶ τὸ μέτωπόν σου χαλ- κοῦν. Καὶ ἀνήγγελκά σοι τὰ
πάλαι πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ἐπὶ σὲ, ἀκουστόν σοι ἐποίησα.9 ∆ιαδείκνυσιν ἐν τούτοις τῆς
ἀνωτάτω φύσεως τὴν ἀπαράβλητον ἡμερότητα, καὶ ὅσον εἰς ἀνθρώπους ποιεῖται
τὸν ἔλεον, καὶ εἴ τινα εἶεν τῶν καταλυπεῖν αὐτὸν εἰωθότων. Ἰσοπαλῆ γὰρ ἔχει τὴν
γαληνότητα τῇ οἰκείᾳ δόξῃ. Καὶ ὥσπερ ἀμέτροις ὑπεροχαῖς τὸ τῶν γενητῶν 374 ὑπερνήχεται μέτρον, οὕτως ἐστὶ καὶ ἀσυγκρίτως φιλάνθρωπος. Ἄθρει γὰρ ὅπως,
καίτοι σκληρὸν ὄντα τὸν Ἰσραὴλ γινώσκων, γαῦρόν τε καὶ ἀπερίθραυστον ἔχοντα

pass_a_gloss: [...] the priests in the [holy] temple singing about Jerusalem: Glorious things were spoken about you, the city of God. The Lord himself also recalls this, saying that some must not swear by their own head, because they cannot make one hair white or black; nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great king. For they were swearing by Jerusalem, naming it, as I said, a city of God. And they were also leaning upon him, saying that the Lord of the powers was their strength. But it was necessary that those who had then supposed it was so should not profane the city of God with altars and sacrifices, being held fast by the deceits of the demons, nor provoke against themselves the one upon whom they had trusted, but rather gladden him with good pursuits, and bringing to him as some sacrifice the fixed [firmness] toward piety. But hear these things, he says; and what sort are these? The former things I announced yet, from my mouth it went out, and it became heard. Suddenly I did, and it came on. For since, as I said, at the beginnings the God-hated Manasseh, having gathered from everywhere the so-called knowers and bird-watchers, was always prying into the future, and having been carried away by their charlatan tricks, he thought perhaps also to know it clearly; for this reason the God of all says: I announced to you the first things too, and not by some other of the falsely named gods were these spoken to you, but from my mouth it went out; and it became heard by you, and suddenly I did, and it came on, that is, even if you did not expect these things to come to an end, yet you knew through the things themselves and the very experience that I both did and it came on. And he seems to say former the misery brought upon them from the war, when, having been carried off from the [land] that bore them, and having taken the yoke of bitter slavery, they were being carried away into the country of Persians and Medes. For second after those things happened to the Babylonians the things brought on them from divine wrath, which also have already been told us through very many words. [Lemma, Isaiah 48:4-5:] I know that you are hard, and your neck an iron sinew, and your forehead bronze. And I have announced to you the things of old before coming upon you, I made it heard to you. He shows in these the incomparable gentleness of the highest nature, and how much mercy it makes toward men, even if some should be of those accustomed to grieve him greatly. For it has the calmness equally matched to its own glory. And just as with measureless pre-eminences it swims above the measure of the things that came to be, so it is also incomparably loving to man. For look how, although knowing Israel to be hard, and having a haughty and unbreakable neck, so that even [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …temple, when the ministering priests sang of Jerusalem: “Glorious things have been spoken of you, O city of God” (Psalm 87:3). The Lord Himself also recalls this, when He says that no one should swear by his own head, because he cannot make one hair white or black, nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King (Matthew 5:35-36). For they used to swear by Jerusalem, calling it, as I said, the city of God. And they leaned on Him too, saying that the Lord of hosts was their strength (compare Isaiah 48:2).

But those who then held this belief ought not to have profaned the city of God with altars and sacrifices, entangled as they were in the deceits of demons, nor to have provoked against themselves the One in whom they trusted; rather they should have gladdened Him with good pursuits, bringing Him, like a sacrifice, a steadfast devotion.

Yet “hear these things,” He says (Isaiah 48:1). And what are they? “The former things I declared long ago; they went out of my mouth and were made known. Suddenly I did them, and they came to pass” (Isaiah 48:3). For, as I said, in the beginning Manasseh, hateful to God, gathered from everywhere the so-called diviners and augurs (compare 2 Kings 21:6) and was always prying into the future; carried away by their charlatan tricks, he perhaps thought that he knew it clearly. That is why the God of all says: It was I who declared to you the first things too; these were not spoken to you by any other of the falsely named gods, but went out of My mouth; it was made known to you, and suddenly I did it, and it came. That is, even if you did not expect these things to come to fulfillment, still you learned through the events themselves and by actual experience that I both did it and it came.

He seems to call “former” the misery brought on them by the war, when they were carried off from their native land, took up the yoke of bitter slavery, and were taken away into the country of the Persians and Medes. For it was second, after those events, that the things brought on the Babylonians by divine wrath befell them, which we have already described at great length.
“I know that you are hard, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead bronze. And I declared to you of old, before it came upon you; I made it known to you” (Isaiah 48:4-5).

Here he shows the incomparable gentleness of the supreme nature, and how great the mercy it shows to human beings, even to those who are used to grieving Him deeply. For its calm forbearance matches its own glory. And just as by boundless excellence it rises far above the measure of created things, so too it is beyond comparison in its love for humankind. choices.why: ἀραρός, fitted and firm; firmness in piety offered like a sacrifice.
βωμολοχία, the low tricks of a buffoon; Cyril's scorn for the diviners.
Isaiah 48:3 Septuagint: God acted without warning.
Literally 'swims above'; God's nature surpasses created measure.
